info.title: Meteor Debris Watch API
info.description: Fireball / bolide detections and maritime exposure assessment for the meteor domain.

get.description: Fetch atmospheric fireball / bolide detections from the NASA/JPL Fireball Data API. Returns located events only, newest first, as `signature`, `count`, `fields`, and `data` (each row's values align to `fields`: date, energy, impact-e, lat, lat-dir, lon, lon-dir, alt, vel). Use whenever the user asks about recent fireballs, bolides, meteor detections, or atmospheric impact events. The response feeds the fireball map, list, and detail widgets directly.

parameters.name: energy_min
parameters.description: Minimum total radiated energy in 10^10 joules (string number, e.g. '5').

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of detections to return (default '50').

200.description: Fireball detections in NASA/JPL Fireball Data API format.

get.description: Fetch the latest NASA/JPL fireball detections and return them as a KML file with one 100 km circle polygon per event. The response is a downloadable `fireballs.kml` suitable for Google Earth or any GIS tool. Accepts the same date and energy filters as get_fireballs.

parameters.name: energy_min
parameters.description: Minimum total radiated energy in 10^10 joules (e.g. '5').

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of fireball detections to include (default '50').

200.description: KML document with one polygon per fireball detection.

get.description: Return the watched maritime fleet, each vessel with `id`, `name`, `latitude`, and `longitude`. Use to overlay vessels on a fireball map or to assess which assets fall within an event's hazard range zones.

post.description: Given a fireball detection set (the get_fireballs response) and a list of vessels (the list_vessels output), return which vessels fall inside a detection's hazard range zones, each tagged with its criticality (critical/high/medium/low), plus an overall threatScore, affectedAssetCount, and estimatedRiskReductionPercent. Use after fetching fireballs and vessels to decide whether to alert the operator and to populate the response-approval widget.

Request operator approval for a recommended response to a meteor / debris event. The operator reviews the situation and either approves, rejects, or requests more analysis. Call this as the final step once you have a recommended set of actions for a threatened event.

source.description: Data source, e.g. 'NASA/JPL Fireball Data API'.

count.description: Number of records returned, as a string.

fields.description: Column names aligned to each data row: date, energy, impact-e, lat, lat-dir, lon, lon-dir, alt, vel.

data.description: Rows of fireball detections; each value aligns to `fields`. Cells may be null (e.g. missing velocity).

destination.description: The vessel's current voyage destination, used to compute a reroute.

vessels.description: Vessels to test against the fireball hazard zones.

criticality.description: Severity of the most-severe zone the vessel falls within.

nearestEventId.description: Identifier (date) of the fireball driving this vessel's criticality.

distanceKm.description: Distance from the vessel to that fireball (km).

safeWaypoint.description: A detour waypoint positioned just outside the hazard zone, on the side away from the fireball. Pass this as a viaPoint to voyage_generate_route so the new route steers clear of the zone. Absent when the vessel has no destination.

affectedVessels.description: Vessels inside at least one hazard zone.

estimatedRiskReductionPercent.description: Estimated risk reduction if recommended actions are taken (0–100).

worstEventId.description: Identifier of the fireball driving the worst exposure, or null if none.

summary.description: One-line human summary of the exposure.

decision.description: The operator's decision on the recommended response.

eventId.description: Identifier of the event the decision relates to.
Identifier of the event the decision relates to.

recordedAt.description: ISO timestamp the decision was recorded.
